In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

.

Tafsir of Surat al-Buruj

It is Meccan.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿By the sky, containing the constellations﴾. That is: the great stars.

ʿIkrimah said: "Containing the palaces."

It is also said: "Containing the beautiful creation." It is also said: "Containing the mansions," which are the mansions of the moon, and they are twenty-eight mansions, as we mentioned earlier.
And His saying: ﴿By the promised day﴾, which is the Day of Resurrection by consensus.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 85, verse 3:

And His saying: ﴿By the witness and the witnessed﴾ — there are several opinions about it. Abu Ishaq narrated from al-Harith, from ʿAli (may Allah be pleased with him) that the witness is the day of Friday (yawm al-jumʿa), and the witnessed is the day of ʿArafa.

He (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Abu Muhammad ʿAbd Allah ibn Muhammad al-Sarifini informed us of this report, saying: Abu al-Qasim ibn Hababa informed us, saying: Abu al-Qasim al-Baghawi informed us, from ʿAli ibn al-Jaʿd, from Sharik, from [Abu] Ishaq.

The report.

The second opinion: the witness is the day of sacrifice (yawm al-nahr), and the witnessed is the day of ʿArafa. This was said by Ibrahim al-Nakhaʿi.

The third opinion: the witness is the angels, and the witnessed is the human being. This was said by al-Suddi.

The fourth opinion: the witness is Muhammad (ﷺ), and the witnessed is the Day of Resurrection. This is narrated from al-Hasan ibn ʿAli, Ibn ʿUmar, and Ibn al-Zubayr (may Allah be pleased with them all).

The fifth opinion: the witness is Allah, and the witnessed is the Day of Resurrection.

The sixth opinion: the witness is ʿIsa ibn Maryam, and the witnessed is the Day of Resurrection.

The seventh opinion: the witness is the limbs (al-jawarih), and the witnessed is the human being's own self.

The eighth opinion: the witness is the day of Monday, and the witnessed is the day of Friday. The witnessing of the days is their testimony over the deeds, and the meaning of "witnessed" regarding the days is that people witness them; and on the Day of Resurrection it means that the angels and all creation witness it.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 85, verse 4:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Killed were the companions of the trench﴾. Al-Ukhdud is the plural of ukhdud (trench), and it is a cleft in the earth. They differed about who this verse was revealed concerning.

ʿAli said: It concerns a people from Habasha (Abyssinia). It is narrated from Mujahid: It concerns a people from Najran. It is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas: It concerns a people from Yemen. It is narrated from some of them: a people from Rum (the Byzantines). And it has been said other than that.

In the tafsir it is mentioned: There was in Najran a people upon the shariʿa (law) of ʿIsa ibn Maryam, upon him be blessings from Allah, who professed tawhid (the oneness of God). Dhu Nuwas came to them and summoned them — and he was one of the kings of Yemen — and gave them the choice between Judaism and being burned by fire. They chose being burned by fire. So he dug for them a trench, set fire in it, and commanded them to become Jews or cast themselves into it. They cast themselves into it until they were burned.

In some of the tafsirs it is mentioned: that among the last of them was a woman with a suckling infant. When she reached the fire, she hesitated, and the child spoke and said: "O mother, go forward and do not hesitate, for it is only a brief moment."

Muslim has mentioned in his Sahih a lengthy account concerning this, and Abu ʿIsa (al-Tirmidhi) too, in a form other than what we have mentioned. Both of them mentioned the hadith of the king, the monk and the sorcerer, which is what is narrated from Thabit al-Bunani, from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from Suhayb, who said: "When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prayed the ʿAsr prayer, he would whisper (hamasa), and the hams in some of their usage is moving the lips as if speaking. It was said to him: O Messenger of Allah, when you pray ʿAsr you whisper. He said: A prophet among the prophets was amazed at his community. Who will stand up for these people? So Allah revealed to him that he should give them the choice between that I take vengeance upon them or that I give their enemy power over them. They chose vengeance, so He gave death power over them, and seventy thousand of them died in a single day."

He said: And whenever he narrated this hadith, he would narrate this other hadith as well. He said: There was a king among the kings, and that king had a soothsayer who would foretell for him. The soothsayer said: "Look for me a boy who is intelligent (fahm) and quick-witted (fatin laqfa), and teach him this knowledge of mine, for I fear that I shall die and this knowledge will be cut off from you, and there will be no one among you who knows it."

He said: So they searched for him according to what he described, and they ordered that he attend that soothsayer and frequent him.

He said: So he began to frequent him, and on the boy's path there was a monk in a hermitage. (Maʿmar said: I think the people of the hermitages were Muslims at that time.) He said: The boy would ask that monk whenever he passed by him, and he continued with him until the monk informed him, and he said: "I worship only Allah." He said: The boy would remain with the monk and be late in returning to the soothsayer, so the soothsayer sent to the boy's family: "He hardly comes to me." The boy informed the monk of this, and the monk said to him: "When the soothsayer says to you, 'Where were you?', say, 'With my family.' And when your family says to you, 'Where were you?', tell them that you were with the soothsayer."

He said: While the boy was in this state, he passed by a large crowd of people whom a beast had blocked — and some of them said: the beast was a lion. He said: So the boy took a stone and said: "O Allah, if what the monk says is true, I ask You to kill it." Then he threw it and killed the beast.

The people said: "Who killed it?" They said: "The boy." The people were alarmed and said: "This boy has knowledge that no one else has."

He said: A blind man heard of him and said to him: "If you restore my sight, you will have such-and-such."

He said to him: "I do not want that from you, but if you stipulate that when your sight returns you will believe in the One who restored it to you, will you do so?" He said: So he called upon Allah, and his sight was returned to him, and the blind man believed.

The king learned of their affair, so he sent for them and they were brought. He said: "I will surely kill each one of you with a killing by which I will not kill his companion." So he ordered the monk and the man who had been blind, and placed the saw on the middle of the head of one of them and killed him, and killed the other with another kind of killing. Then he ordered the boy and said: "Take him to such-and-such mountain and throw him down from its summit." When they reached the place from which they intended to throw him, they began to fall and perish from that mountain, until none of them remained except the boy.

He said: Then he returned, and the king ordered that they take him to the sea and cast him into it. They went to the sea, and Allah drowned those who were with him and saved him. The boy said: "You will not kill me until you crucify me and shoot me, and say when you shoot me: 'In the name of Allah, Lord of this boy.'"

He said: So he ordered that he be crucified, then shot him, and said: "In the name of Allah, Lord of this boy."

He said: The boy placed his hand on his temple when he was shot, and then died. The people said: "This boy has known a knowledge that no one has known. We believe in the Lord of the boy."

He said: It was said to the king: "Are you distressed that three have opposed you? Here are all the people who have opposed you."

He said: So he dug a trench, then placed firewood and fire in it, then gathered the people.

He said: "Whoever turns back from his religion, we will leave him; and whoever does not turn back, we will throw him into this fire." So he began throwing them into that trench.

He said: Allah, may He be exalted, says: ﴿Killed were the companions of the trench, the fire full of fuel﴾ up to ﴿the Lord of the Throne, the Glorious﴾.

He said: As for the boy, he was buried. It is mentioned that he was brought out in the time of ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, with his finger on his temple just as he had placed it when he was killed.

Abu ʿIsa said: A hadith, hasan gharib (sahih).

He, may Allah be pleased with him, said: This hadith was reported to us by Abu ʿAbd al-Rahman Ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Ahmad, who said: Abu al-ʿAbbas ibn Siraj reported to us, Abu al-ʿAbbas al-Mahbubi reported to us, ʿAbd al-Razzaq reported to us, from Maʿmar... the report.

Muslim also mentioned this report in his book, and differed from it in other places.

In some narrations, the name of that boy was ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Tamir.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: In the time of ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him), a pit was dug, and they found ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Tamir with his hand on his temple. Whenever they moved his hand away from that place, blood would gush out, and when they left the hand, it returned to its place. On his finger was an iron ring inscribed: "My Lord is Allah." So ʿUmar ordered that he be returned to that place just as he was found.

It is narrated from al-Hasan al-Basri that the Prophet (ﷺ), whenever he mentioned this story, would say: "O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the severity of calamity."

Some of the scholars of meanings (ahl al-maʿani) mentioned that His saying ﴿Killed were the companions of the trench﴾ is the answer to the oath.

His saying: ﴿the fire, full of fuel﴾. According to the view that it is a *badal* (apposition) of *al-Ukhdud* (the trench), it is as if he said: "The companions of the trench were killed: the fire, full of fuel." *Al-wuqud* is that with which the fire is kindled. It was also said that *dhat al-wuqud* means *dhat al-tawaqqud* (that which is blazing), and this is the more correct view.
"His saying: ﴿While they were sitting over it﴾ means: seated. And in the narrative, the king and his companions had sat on thrones beside the trenches."
And His saying: ﴿And they were witnesses to what they were doing to the believers﴾ — he did what he did to the believers in their presence.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 85, verse 8:

And His saying: ﴿They did not resent them for anything except that they believed in Allah, the Almighty, the Praiseworthy﴾. Ibn ʿAbbās said: "They did not dislike (them)."

And from others: "They did not find fault with (them)."

Al-Zajjāj mentioned: "They did not deny (them)."

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Qays (ibn) al-Ruqayyāt said:

(They resented nothing in the Banū Umayyah except that they bear (burdens) when they are angry,)

(and that they are the lords of kings, so none fit to rule are the Arabs except over them.)

And His saying: ﴿except that they believe in Allah, the Almighty, the Praiseworthy﴾. The meaning is that they did not deny anything against them except their belief in Allah.

.

And His saying: ﴿the Almighty, the Praiseworthy﴾, i.e., the Overpowering by His might, the Praiseworthy in His actions.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 85, verse 9:

Allah's saying: ﴿He to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. And Allah is, over all things, Witness.﴾ The meaning is apparent.

Al-Zajjaj (ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq al-Zajjaj, d. 311 AH, Qur'anic grammarian and exegete) said: The purpose of the verse is that Allah, exalted is He, mentioned a people whose insight into the religion had reached the point that they were given the choice between disbelief and being burned in fire, so they endured patiently until they were burned in the fire.

It has been reported in some traditions from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Do not associate anything with Allah, even if you are killed and burned."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 85, verse 10:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, those who persecuted the believing men and believing women﴾ — meaning: they burned them. It is said: "fatantu al-dhahab bil-nar" (I smelted the gold in the fire) when I put it into it; and it is said: "harrah fatin" (a black stone-land, fatin) when it is black, as if burnt. ﴿Then they did not repent, so for them is the punishment of Hell, and for them is the punishment of the Burning﴾ — the punishment of Hell for their disbelief, and a kind of punishment for their burning of the believers.

It is narrated from al-Rabi' ibn Anas that the fire in which they burned the believers rose up from the trench (al-ukhdud), and it burned the king and his companions. This is the meaning of His words: ﴿And for them is the punishment of the Burning﴾.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds will have gardens beneath which rivers flow. That is the great triumph.﴾ "The great" means "the magnificent." This is in keeping with the manner of the Qur'an: when it mentions the promise to the disbelievers, it mentions the promise to the believers alongside it, and this is evident in most of the Qur'an.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 85, verse 12:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, the seizing of your Lord is severe.﴾ Al-batsh (the seizing) is taking with violence and force.
Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, it is He who originates and repeats.﴾ That is, He originates creation in this world, then He brings them back again in the Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 85, verse 14:

The words of the Most High: ﴿And He is the All-Forgiving, the Most Loving﴾. Al-Ghafur (the All-Forgiving) is the One who conceals the sins of His servants. Al-Wadud (the Most Loving) is the One who loves the believers. It was also said: the one who shows affection toward the believers through His beautiful acts and abundant kindness.

Al-Azhari mentioned that it is permissible for al-Wadud to be in the sense of mawdud (the one who is loved), like halub and rukub in the sense of mahlub and marku b (the one milked and the one ridden). According to this, in His words ﴿al-Wadud﴾ there are two meanings. The first: He is the One who loves His believing servants.

The second: the One whom the believers love.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 85, verse 15:

And His words: ﴿Owner of the Throne, the Glorious﴾. Most of the readers recited it with a raised vowel (ar-raf'), while Hamzah and al-Kisa'i recited it with a lowered vowel (al-khafd).

Al-'Arsh (the throne) linguistically means a couch (sarir). As for in the Qur'an, it is the well-known Throne above the heavens.

In tafsir, it is said: He whose measure cannot be estimated (by anyone).

It is reported from some of them: "Dhu al-'Arsh" means "Dhu al-Mulk" (Owner of the dominion). It is said: "Kull 'arsh fulan" meaning "the dominion of so-and-so," and it is said: "Tabawwa'a fulan 'ala sarir mulkihi," meaning "so-and-so's dominion was established," even if there was no couch at that time. This was related by al-Qaffal, but the correct view is the first one.

As for the raised reading, it is an attribute of God Most High, meaning exaltedness and greatness. As for the lowered reading, there are several views: First, that it is an attribute of the Throne, and the meaning of "al-Majid" in it is the elevated, the lofty. The second view: that it is an attribute of God Most High, but it is lowered by proximity (bi-l-jiwar). The third view: that it refers back to His words ﴿Indeed, the seizure of your Lord﴾, as if He said: "Indeed the seizure of your Lord, the Glorious, is severe." This was cited by al-Nahhas.

It is reported from some of them that the answer to the oath is His words ﴿Indeed, the seizure of your Lord is severe﴾, and this is the view of the majority.

The Almighty's words: ﴿Doer of what He intends﴾, meaning: He does whatever He wills and chooses.

It is related in some reports that Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, fell ill, and people entered to visit him. They said to him: "Shall we not call a physician for you?" He said: "I have already called him."

They said: "And what did he say?" Abu Bakr said: "He said: 'I am the doer of what I intend.'"
Exalted is He said: ﴿Has the story of the hosts reached you?﴾ That is, "Indeed, I have come to you with the report of the hosts."

The commentary on the verse ﴿Pharaoh and Thamud﴾ (85:18):

And His saying: ﴿Pharaoh and Thamud﴾, meaning: the armies of Pharaoh and Thamud.

Al-Naqqash mentioned that when Pharaoh pursued the Children of Israel, they (his armies) numbered five thousand and five hundred thousand.

.

Wa qawluhu: ﴿Bal alladhina kafaru fi takdhib﴾ ay fi takdhib al-rusul.

Translation:

And His saying: ﴿Nay, those who disbelieve are in denial﴾ means: in denying the messengers.

Surah 85, verse 20. The Qur'anic quotation is ﴿وَالله من وَرَاءَهُمْ مُحِيط﴾ — translate its meaning inside the markers.

And His saying: ﴿And Allah, from behind them, is all-encompassing﴾, meaning: encompassing their deeds and their words.

The Qur'an verse ﴿Rather, it is a glorious Qur'an﴾. In some exegeses it is reported that when the Messenger (ﷺ) recited to them the verses we mentioned, they said to him: "Perhaps you have made a mistake or forgotten? Perhaps what is being revealed to you is not from God?" So God Most High revealed ﴿Rather, it is a glorious Qur'an﴾. "Majid" (glorious) means one who is gathered together with all the qualities of goodness.

And Muhammad al-Yamami recited it as "Bal huwa Qur'anun majid" with an idafah (construct), meaning "a Qur'an of a Glorious Lord."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 85, verse 22:

And His saying: ﴿In a Preserved Tablet﴾ has been recited with both the nominative (raf') and the genitive (khafd), each with tanwin. In the nominative, it refers to the Qur'an; in the genitive, it refers to the Tablet (al-lawh).

Sa'id ibn Jubayr narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that the Preserved Tablet is of white pearl; its two covers are of red ruby; its writing is light, and its pen is light. Allah looks into it every day three hundred and sixty looks. He gives life and causes death, bestows honour and brings humiliation, makes poor and makes rich, and does whatever He wills.

In some reports: it is written on its front, "There is no god but Allah, alone, without partner; there is no god but Allah; Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah."

The mention of preservation (al-hifz) here is to show that what is revealed to him (ﷺ) of the Qur'an is preserved from forgetfulness and error, and that what the Prophet (ﷺ) says, he says from Allah, glorified and exalted is He.

And it is related from Farqad al-Sabakhi that His saying ﴿In a Preserved Tablet﴾ refers to the heart of the believer. This is a weak opinion, and Allah knows best.
